dimensions.label: Competent, independent, impartial tribunal established by law
dimensions.standard: The adjudicating tribunal must be competent, independent, impartial and established by law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law.
dimensions.exceptions: An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.
questions: What law establishes the tribunal's authority?

dimensions.applicability: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law. An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.

dimensions.label: Equality before courts and equality of arms
dimensions.standard: Equality before courts and tribunals requires equal access and procedural opportunities; distinctions require objective, reasonable justification without actual disadvantage or unfairness.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law.
dimensions.exceptions: Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.
questions: Could the parties access the tribunal and make submissions?
Did disclosure, resources or procedure put one party at material disadvantage, with what justification?
dimensions.applicability: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law. Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.

dimensions.label: Public hearings and public judgments
dimensions.standard: Hearings and judgments must ordinarily be public; permitted exclusions and judgment exceptions require case-specific justification.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.

Was the judgment made public, subject to applicable exceptions?

dimensions.label: Presumption of innocence
dimensions.standard: Everyone charged with a criminal offence is presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law; the prosecution bears the burden and authorities must refrain from prejudging guilt.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through adjudication.
dimensions.exceptions: Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.
questions: Who bore the burden and what proof standard was used?
Did authorities prejudge guilt or present the accused as guilty?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through adjudication. Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.

dimensions.label: Notice of charges
dimensions.standard: Prompt, detailed notice in a language understood of the nature and cause of the criminal charge.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges.
dimensions.exceptions: Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.
questions: When did the person learn the charge and alleged acts?
What details and language were provided?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges. Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.

dimensions.label: Adequate time and facilities for defence
dimensions.standard: Adequate time and facilities to prepare the defence, including access to relevant documents and other evidence needed for defence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps.
dimensions.exceptions: Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.
questions: What preparation time, case complexity and disclosure were available?
Were necessary adjournments/access requested and how were requests decided?
dimensions.applicability: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps. Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.

dimensions.label: Access to effective legal assistance
dimensions.standard: Defence in person or through legal assistance of choice, confidential access to counsel, and assigned effective assistance where justice requires subject to means conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal defence; distinguish custodial/investigation guarantees under Article 9 and applicable domestic law.
dimensions.exceptions: Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.
questions: Was counsel chosen/assigned, accessible and confidential?

Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.

dimensions.label: Presence and meaningful participation
dimensions.standard: An accused ordinarily has a right to be tried in their presence and meaningfully defend the case.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and defence participation.
dimensions.exceptions: Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.
questions: Was the accused present, informed and able to follow/respond?
If absent or restricted, what notice/opportunity and reasons existed?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal trial and defence participation. Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.

dimensions.label: Examine witnesses and present defence evidence
dimensions.standard: Examine prosecution witnesses and obtain/examine defence witnesses under the same conditions; meaningful opportunity to challenge material evidence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and material defence evidence requests.
dimensions.exceptions: This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.
questions: Could material prosecution witnesses/evidence be challenged?
Could relevant defence witnesses/evidence be presented under comparable conditions?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal trial and material defence evidence requests. This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.

dimensions.label: Interpretation where required
dimensions.standard: Free assistance of an interpreter where the accused cannot understand or speak the language used in court.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken.

questions: What language ability and proceedings language are documented?

dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken. Nationality or multilingual setting alone does not prove need or adequacy. This right does not require proceedings in the preferred language where the court language is sufficiently understood.

dimensions.label: Protection against compelled self-incrimination
dimensions.standard: No compulsion to testify against oneself or confess guilt; exclude prohibited coercion and examine allegations of involuntary statements.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial.
dimensions.exceptions: Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.
questions: How was the statement obtained and was compulsion alleged?
How did the court handle coercion allegations and use/exclusion?
dimensions.applicability: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial. Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.

dimensions.label: Trial without undue delay
dimensions.standard: Criminal proceedings must proceed without undue delay, assessed from formal charge through final judgment including appeal.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal.
dimensions.exceptions: Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.
questions: What intervals, procedural steps and reasons for delay are documented?
How do complexity, party conduct, court conduct and detention affect adequacy?

dimensions.label: Review of conviction and sentence
dimensions.standard: Conviction and sentence must be reviewed by a higher tribunal according to law, including sufficient substantive review of facts and law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review.
dimensions.exceptions: Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.
questions: Was higher review available and effective for both conviction and sentence?
What facts/law, judgment and record were reviewed and what barriers existed?
dimensions.applicability: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review. Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.

dimensions.label: Conditional juvenile safeguards
dimensions.standard: Proceedings for juveniles must take account of age and the desirability of promoting rehabilitation.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date.
dimensions.exceptions: Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.
questions: What age/status applies at the event date?
What age-appropriate procedure, assistance and rehabilitation/diversion protections were used?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date. Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.

dimensions.label: Conditional protection from double jeopardy
dimensions.standard: No repeated trial or punishment for an offence after final conviction/acquittal under the law and penal procedure of the same country.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence.
dimensions.exceptions: Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.
questions: Was a prior decision final, for the same offence in the same country?
Is this a new prosecution or permitted review/resumption, on what grounds?
dimensions.applicability: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence. Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. dimensions.label: Conditional miscarriage-of-justice compensation

dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction.
dimensions.exceptions: Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.
questions: Do final conviction, punishment, qualifying reversal/pardon and new fact meet the conditions?
What compensation route and non-disclosure exception apply?
dimensions.applicability: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction. Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial.
dimensions.exceptions: Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.
questions: How was the statement obtained and was compulsion alleged?
How did the court handle coercion allegations and use/exclusion?
dimensions.applicability: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial. Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.

dimensions.label: Trial without undue delay
dimensions.standard: Criminal proceedings must proceed without undue delay, assessed from formal charge through final judgment including appeal.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal.
dimensions.exceptions: Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.
questions: What intervals, procedural steps and reasons for delay are documented?
How do complexity, party conduct, court conduct and detention affect adequacy?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal. Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.

dimensions.label: Review of conviction and sentence
dimensions.standard: Conviction and sentence must be reviewed by a higher tribunal according to law, including sufficient substantive review of facts and law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review.
dimensions.exceptions: Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.
questions: Was higher review available and effective for both conviction and sentence?
What facts/law, judgment and record were reviewed and what barriers existed?
dimensions.applicability: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review. Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.

dimensions.label: Conditional juvenile safeguards
dimensions.standard: Proceedings for juveniles must take account of age and the desirability of promoting rehabilitation.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date.
dimensions.exceptions: Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.
questions: What age/status applies at the event date?
What age-appropriate procedure, assistance and rehabilitation/diversion protections were used?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date. Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.

dimensions.label: Conditional protection from double jeopardy
dimensions.standard: No repeated trial or punishment for an offence after final conviction/acquittal under the law and penal procedure of the same country.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence.
dimensions.exceptions: Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.
questions: Was a prior decision final, for the same offence in the same country?
Is this a new prosecution or permitted review/resumption, on what grounds?
dimensions.applicability: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence. Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.

dimensions.label: Conditional miscarriage-of-justice compensation
dimensions.standard: Compensation according to law where a final conviction is reversed or a pardon granted because a new/newly discovered fact conclusively shows miscarriage of justice, subject to non-disclosure conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction.
dimensions.exceptions: Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.
questions: Do final conviction, punishment, qualifying reversal/pardon and new fact meet the conditions?
What compensation route and non-disclosure exception apply?
dimensions.applicability: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction. Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.

dimensions.label: Expression and restrictive interference
dimensions.standard: Identify the expression, whether Article 19 protects it and the specific restriction. Freedom to hold opinions without interference is distinct from expression restrictions.
dimensions.applicability: Do not presume expression was involved in every prosecution. Identify conduct and restriction; Article 20 duties and other rights may also require analysis.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: Do not presume expression was involved in every prosecution. Identify conduct and restriction; Article 20 duties and other rights may also require analysis.
questions: What expression, restriction, law, asserted aim and particular justification are documented?
What competing account or missing facts would change this dimension's assessment?

dimensions.label: Restriction's legal basis
dimensions.standard: Any restriction of protected expression must be provided by law with sufficient precision and accessible guidance; discretion must be bounded.
dimensions.applicability: First establish expression and restriction. Citation of a statute alone does not settle foreseeability or its application.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: First establish expression and restriction. Citation of a statute alone does not settle foreseeability or its application.
questions: What expression, restriction, law, asserted aim and particular justification are documented?
What competing account or missing facts would change this dimension's assessment?

dimensions.label: Asserted legitimate aim
dimensions.standard: Expression restrictions must serve the rights or reputations of others, national security, public order, public health or morals; asserted reasons require attribution and scrutiny.
dimensions.applicability: An asserted aim is a government position, not proof of necessity or legitimacy in the particular application. Missing government reasons remain unknown.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: An asserted aim is a government position, not proof of necessity or legitimacy in the particular application. Missing government reasons remain unknown.
questions: What expression, restriction, law, asserted aim and particular justification are documented?
What competing account or missing facts would change this dimension's assessment?

dimensions.label: Necessity and proportionality
dimensions.standard: A restriction must be necessary and proportionate to a permitted aim, with a specific direct connection between the expression and the threat; examine less intrusive measures.
dimensions.applicability: Assess actual expression, aim, harm, penalty and alternatives. A restriction is not automatically unlawful; a legal basis and aim do not automatically establish necessity.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: Assess actual expression, aim, harm, penalty and alternatives. A restriction is not automatically unlawful; a legal basis and aim do not automatically establish necessity.
questions: What expression, restriction, law, asserted aim and particular justification are documented?
What competing account or missing facts would change this dimension's assessment?

missing_facts: Jurisdictional and assignment records for the RTC case

dimensions.explanation: The judgment identifies the Supreme Court en banc and an RTC judge/branch. Defence resources and assistance during trial and review
Procedural requests, objections, refusals and their effect
dimensions.explanation: The Court records the accused's competing account and counsel-related objection, rather than only the prosecution account. That is affirmative evidence that submissions were considered, but it does not establish comparable disclosure, resources, evidentiary access or opportunity. missing_facts: Actual public access to the trial hearings
Any exclusion order, scope, ground and necessity
Historical publication/access timing and relevant appeal-hearing form
dimensions.explanation: The judgment reports that Mahinay testified in open court, and the reasoned Supreme Court decision is publicly reproduced in the retained source. This supports specific public-facing components, but neither proves the public could attend all relevant trial hearings, that any exclusions were lawful, nor that the judgment was available at its historical issuance. The victim's childhood and privacy concerns could bear on permissible exclusions; they are not proof an exclusion occurred.

missing_facts: Exact setting of the police/reporter interview and whether silence followed warnings
Original RTC reasoning and transcript showing the inference's weight
Defence objection and any separate ruling on use of silence
dimensions.explanation: The Supreme Court reproduces and relies on trial-court reasoning that persistent silence justifies an inference of non-innocence. Treating failure to protest innocence to police or a reporter as an adverse guilt indicator is a substantial documented concern about the presumption and prosecution burden. The score addresses that express reasoning, not guilt or innocence. The contrary evidence is important: the Court states a beyond-reasonable-doubt circumstantial-evidence test, says prosecution evidence cannot draw strength from a weak defence, and finds independent evidence sufficient. Those holdings do not erase the silence-based reasoning, but the source does not establish whether it was decisive, what warnings applied at the particular interview, or whether a treaty violation was adjudicated.
dimensions.next_verification: Have a qualified reviewer compare the original inference, interview circumstances and independent proof with contemporaneous Article III sections 12/14/17 and ICCPR 14(2); reassess if the inference was not applied as reproduced.

missing_facts: Arraignment date and record of service/oral explanation
Language understood and language used for formal notice
Actual Information/charge explanation and delivery timing
dimensions.explanation: The judgment reports an Information filed on 1995-07-10 charging rape with homicide and a not-guilty plea. Formal charging and a plea show that a criminal charge was presented, but do not prove when Mahinay received its nature, legal basis and alleged acts, in what language, or whether the notice was sufficiently prompt and detailed. The Court's later arrest-reasons guideline (JP0228) is a principle, not a finding that notice was actually provided here, and Article 9 arrest reasons are distinct.
dimensions.next_verification: Inspect the retained Information and arraignment/service record if supplied; do not substitute the date of filing for the date the accused learned the charge.

missing_facts: Counsel appointment and actual preparation time
Disclosure of confession, forensic and witness material
Access to exculpatory material and adjournment requests/rulings
dimensions.explanation: The charge was filed in July 1995 and the RTC decision was issued in October 1995, after a trial described in the judgment. Those dates and the ability to advance a competing account do not establish adequate preparation time or facilities. No source describes disclosure, confidential consultation, adjournment requests or access to exculpatory evidence. A roughly three-month filing-to-decision interval can be neither compliance nor undue haste without those facts.
dimensions.next_verification: Inspect preparation/disclosure and consultation records; determine complexity and requests rather than inferring adequacy from elapsed time.

missing_facts: Questioning and conditions from arrest until the lawyer arrived
Original signed warnings/waiver and counsel's complete testimony
Private consultation, actual choice and practical independence
Representation and effectiveness at trial and appeal
dimensions.explanation: Mahinay alleged that counsel assisted only when he was forced to sign a confession. If established, token assistance at signature would not satisfy the contemporaneous custodial-counsel safeguards. This supports a specific possible concern, rather than proof of denial. The Court expressly rejected it, relying on the PAO lawyer's testimony that he explained rights before questioning, was present, and explained the waiver in Tagalog. That is the strongest contrary evidence and must remain visible. The reproduction does not resolve any earlier questioning before counsel arrived, confidential advice, choice/independence in practice, or effectiveness through trial and appeal; PAO employment alone proves neither independence nor its absence.
dimensions.next_verification: Compare the original interrogation chronology, counsel testimony and signed documents with Article III section 12 and RA7438 section 2(a)-(b); keep the accused's version and the Court's contrary finding distinct.
dimensions.applicability: Historical prosecution, custodial statement and trial in 1995, followed by Supreme Court automatic review decided 1999-02-01. Custodial safeguards affect later trial fairness but are not substituted for a full trial-counsel assessment; later GC32 paragraphs 34 and 37-38.

missing_facts: Attendance at all material stages
Any restriction or absence, notice and justification
Understanding and ability to instruct counsel/respond
dimensions.explanation: A not-guilty plea, testimony in open court and presentation of a competing account are documented opportunities to participate. They do not establish attendance or understanding throughout all material hearings, access to counsel when needed, or opportunity to respond to every material allegation. Nothing in the reproduced judgment proves exclusion or an unjustified in-absentia proceeding. An adverse credibility finding about his account is not itself denial of participation.
dimensions.next_verification: Inspect relevant attendance and trial records before treating one documented episode as complete meaningful participation.
dimensions.applicability: Historical prosecution, custodial statement and trial in 1995, followed by Supreme Court automatic review decided 1999-02-01. missing_facts: Cross-examination opportunities and actual scope
Defence witness/evidence requests and rulings
Disclosure and ability to challenge the confession and material witnesses
dimensions.explanation: The accused gave a defence account and contested circumstantial evidence and the confession; the Court addressed these objections. That is evidence of contestation, but the reproduction does not show whether material prosecution witnesses were cross-examined, whether relevant defence witnesses could be secured, or whether exclusion/refusal requests caused disadvantage. The appellate credibility deference is a review method, not proof that confrontation was denied.

dimensions.applicability: Historical prosecution, custodial statement and trial in 1995, followed by Supreme Court automatic review decided 1999-02-01. missing_facts: Courtroom language and accused's documented language ability
Any interpretation request, response and interpreter provision
Coverage and adequacy of interpretation at material proceedings
dimensions.explanation: The quoted lawyer testimony supports explanation of custodial rights/waiver in Filipino/Tagalog. The reproduction also contains Tagalog questions and answers. These facts do not establish courtroom-language ability, an interpreter need, or adequate free interpretation through trial and review. The English-language reproduction is not proof that the accused understood English, and using Tagalog at custody does not prove he could not understand the courtroom language.

missing_facts: Conditions before counsel arrived and investigation of the alleged threat
Original confession, waiver and full voluntariness testimony
Whether medical access was available and why no certificate was produced
The applicable contemporaneous admissibility/burden ruling and whether independent evidence depended on confession
dimensions.explanation: The accused alleged a police threat against his life and a confession signed under pressure; the trial reasoning reproduced by the Court stressed lack of medical proof. A threat can be psychological compulsion without a medical injury, so absence of a certificate alone does not resolve the allegation. This is a specific possible concern about voluntariness/exclusion and the adequacy of investigation, not a finding that police torture occurred. Contrary evidence is strong: the Court found the confession voluntary and accepted counsel's testimony about warnings, presence and an explained waiver. The Court's general exclusion guideline is a safeguard it states, not independent proof of this accused's treatment. Later GC32 paragraph 41 clarifies a State voluntariness burden; it is not presented as a rule newly issued in 1995 or as evidence the contemporaneous court applied it.
dimensions.next_verification: Examine the original voluntariness dispute and the State's safeguard evidence under ICCPR 14(3)(g), Article 7 and Constitution Article III sections 12/17; distinguish lack of corroboration from positive proof no coercion occurred.

Missing evidence is unknown.

scale.0: Affirmative relevant evidence documents a safeguard/no specific concern on this assessed dimension. Missing documents cannot produce zero; this is not certification of full compliance.
scale.1: Specific possible concern; a material factual or legal explanation remains unresolved.
scale.2: Substantial documented concern: cited propositions strongly indicate a departure from the standard; competing accounts and unresolved justification remain visible.
scale.3: Severe documented concern: explanation explicitly addresses gravity, duration or centrality and strongest available support; this remains provisional, not a legal finding.

dimensions.label: Competent, independent, impartial tribunal established by law
dimensions.standard: The adjudicating tribunal must be competent, independent, impartial and established by law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law.
dimensions.exceptions: An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.
questions: What law establishes the tribunal's authority?
What evidence addresses competence, interference, conflicts or objective appearance of bias?
dimensions.applicability: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law. An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.

dimensions.label: Equality before courts and equality of arms
dimensions.standard: Equality before courts and tribunals requires equal access and procedural opportunities; distinctions require objective, reasonable justification without actual disadvantage or unfairness.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law.
dimensions.exceptions: Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.
questions: Could the parties access the tribunal and make submissions?
Did disclosure, resources or procedure put one party at material disadvantage, with what justification?
dimensions.applicability: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law. Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.

dimensions.label: Public hearings and public judgments
dimensions.standard: Hearings and judgments must ordinarily be public; permitted exclusions and judgment exceptions require case-specific justification.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Hearing and judgment in determination of a criminal charge or suit at law; determine hearing type, as not every pretrial/appeal step requires a public hearing.
dimensions.exceptions: Press/public may be excluded for morals, public order, national security in a democratic society, private lives, or strictly necessary special circumstances where publicity prejudices justice. Judgment exceptions include juvenile interests or matrimonial/child guardianship disputes.
questions: Was the hearing open to the public, and were any exclusions justified?
Was the judgment made public, subject to applicable exceptions?
components: Exception justification; missing web copies are evidence gaps, not proof
dimensions.applicability: Hearing and judgment in determination of a criminal charge or suit at law; determine hearing type, as not every pretrial/appeal step requires a public hearing. Press/public may be excluded for morals, public order, national security in a democratic society, private lives, or strictly necessary special circumstances where publicity prejudices justice. Judgment exceptions include juvenile interests or matrimonial/child guardianship disputes.

dimensions.label: Presumption of innocence
dimensions.standard: Everyone charged with a criminal offence is presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law; the prosecution bears the burden and authorities must refrain from prejudging guilt.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through adjudication.
dimensions.exceptions: Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.
questions: Who bore the burden and what proof standard was used?
Did authorities prejudge guilt or present the accused as guilty?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through adjudication. Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.

dimensions.label: Notice of charges
dimensions.standard: Prompt, detailed notice in a language understood of the nature and cause of the criminal charge.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges.
dimensions.exceptions: Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.
questions: When did the person learn the charge and alleged acts?
What details and language were provided?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges. Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.

dimensions.label: Adequate time and facilities for defence
dimensions.standard: Adequate time and facilities to prepare the defence, including access to relevant documents and other evidence needed for defence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps.
dimensions.exceptions: Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.
questions: What preparation time, case complexity and disclosure were available?
Were necessary adjournments/access requested and how were requests decided?
dimensions.applicability: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps. Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.

dimensions.label: Access to effective legal assistance
dimensions.standard: Defence in person or through legal assistance of choice, confidential access to counsel, and assigned effective assistance where justice requires subject to means conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal defence; distinguish custodial/investigation guarantees under Article 9 and applicable domestic law.
dimensions.exceptions: Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.
questions: Was counsel chosen/assigned, accessible and confidential?
Were required assistance and effective representation available, with what restrictions?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal defence; distinguish custodial/investigation guarantees under Article 9 and applicable domestic law. Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.

dimensions.label: Presence and meaningful participation
dimensions.standard: An accused ordinarily has a right to be tried in their presence and meaningfully defend the case.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and defence participation.
dimensions.exceptions: Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.
questions: Was the accused present, informed and able to follow/respond?
If absent or restricted, what notice/opportunity and reasons existed?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal trial and defence participation. Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.

dimensions.label: Examine witnesses and present defence evidence
dimensions.standard: Examine prosecution witnesses and obtain/examine defence witnesses under the same conditions; meaningful opportunity to challenge material evidence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and material defence evidence requests.
dimensions.exceptions: This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.
questions: Could material prosecution witnesses/evidence be challenged?
Could relevant defence witnesses/evidence be presented under comparable conditions?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal trial and material defence evidence requests. This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.

dimensions.label: Interpretation where required
dimensions.standard: Free assistance of an interpreter where the accused cannot understand or speak the language used in court.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken.
dimensions.exceptions: Nationality or multilingual setting alone does not prove need or adequacy. This right does not require proceedings in the preferred language where the court language is sufficiently understood.
questions: What language ability and proceedings language are documented?
Was free, adequate interpretation provided throughout relevant proceedings?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken. Nationality or multilingual setting alone does not prove need or adequacy. This right does not require proceedings in the preferred language where the court language is sufficiently understood.

dimensions.label: Protection against compelled self-incrimination
dimensions.standard: No compulsion to testify against oneself or confess guilt; exclude prohibited coercion and examine allegations of involuntary statements.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial.
dimensions.exceptions: Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.
questions: How was the statement obtained and was compulsion alleged?
How did the court handle coercion allegations and use/exclusion?
dimensions.applicability: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial. Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.

dimensions.label: Trial without undue delay
dimensions.standard: Criminal proceedings must proceed without undue delay, assessed from formal charge through final judgment including appeal.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal.
dimensions.exceptions: Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.
questions: What intervals, procedural steps and reasons for delay are documented?
How do complexity, party conduct, court conduct and detention affect adequacy?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal. Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.

dimensions.label: Review of conviction and sentence
dimensions.standard: Conviction and sentence must be reviewed by a higher tribunal according to law, including sufficient substantive review of facts and law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review.
dimensions.exceptions: Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.
questions: Was higher review available and effective for both conviction and sentence?
What facts/law, judgment and record were reviewed and what barriers existed?
dimensions.applicability: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review. Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.

dimensions.label: Conditional juvenile safeguards
dimensions.standard: Proceedings for juveniles must take account of age and the desirability of promoting rehabilitation.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date.
dimensions.exceptions: Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.
questions: What age/status applies at the event date?
What age-appropriate procedure, assistance and rehabilitation/diversion protections were used?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date. Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.

dimensions.label: Conditional protection from double jeopardy
dimensions.standard: No repeated trial or punishment for an offence after final conviction/acquittal under the law and penal procedure of the same country.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence.
dimensions.exceptions: Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.
questions: Was a prior decision final, for the same offence in the same country?
Is this a new prosecution or permitted review/resumption, on what grounds?
dimensions.applicability: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence. Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.

dimensions.label: Conditional miscarriage-of-justice compensation
dimensions.standard: Compensation according to law where a final conviction is reversed or a pardon granted because a new/newly discovered fact conclusively shows miscarriage of justice, subject to non-disclosure conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction.
dimensions.exceptions: Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.
questions: Do final conviction, punishment, qualifying reversal/pardon and new fact meet the conditions?
What compensation route and non-disclosure exception apply?
dimensions.applicability: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction. Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.

dimensions.label: Expression and restrictive interference
dimensions.standard: Identify the expression, whether Article 19 protects it and the specific restriction. Freedom to hold opinions without interference is distinct from expression restrictions.
dimensions.applicability: Do not presume expression was involved in every prosecution. Identify conduct and restriction; Article 20 duties and other rights may also require analysis.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: Do not presume expression was involved in every prosecution. Identify conduct and restriction; Article 20 duties and other rights may also require analysis.
questions: What expression, restriction, law, asserted aim and particular justification are documented?
What competing account or missing facts would change this dimension's assessment?

dimensions.label: Restriction's legal basis
dimensions.standard: Any restriction of protected expression must be provided by law with sufficient precision and accessible guidance; discretion must be bounded.
dimensions.applicability: First establish expression and restriction. Citation of a statute alone does not settle foreseeability or its application.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: First establish expression and restriction. Citation of a statute alone does not settle foreseeability or its application.
questions: What expression, restriction, law, asserted aim and particular justification are documented?
What competing account or missing facts would change this dimension's assessment?

dimensions.label: Asserted legitimate aim
dimensions.standard: Expression restrictions must serve the rights or reputations of others, national security, public order, public health or morals; asserted reasons require attribution and scrutiny.
dimensions.applicability: An asserted aim is a government position, not proof of necessity or legitimacy in the particular application. Missing government reasons remain unknown.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: An asserted aim is a government position, not proof of necessity or legitimacy in the particular application. Missing government reasons remain unknown.
questions: What expression, restriction, law, asserted aim and particular justification are documented?
What competing account or missing facts would change this dimension's assessment?

dimensions.label: Necessity and proportionality
dimensions.standard: A restriction must be necessary and proportionate to a permitted aim, with a specific direct connection between the expression and the threat; examine less intrusive measures.
dimensions.applicability: Assess actual expression, aim, harm, penalty and alternatives. A restriction is not automatically unlawful; a legal basis and aim do not automatically establish necessity.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: Assess actual expression, aim, harm, penalty and alternatives. A restriction is not automatically unlawful; a legal basis and aim do not automatically establish necessity.
questions: What expression, restriction, law, asserted aim and particular justification are documented?
What competing account or missing facts would change this dimension's assessment?

rubric.completeness_method: Analyst judgment of relevant factual/legal coverage for this dimension; missing information is unknown.
rubric.limits: No combined percentage, calibrated probability, official TrialWatch grade or definitive violation finding. Country indicators cannot change individual scores. This is a partial rubric, not an exhaustive legal checklist.

Case-specific objective independence and impartiality evidence
upgrade_dimensions.explanation: The judgment identifies the Supreme Court en banc and an RTC judge/branch. The strong condemnatory language in a final judgment and an adverse outcome alone do not prove prejudgment or institutional bias.

missing_facts: Disclosure and access to prosecution/exculpatory materials
Defence resources and assistance during trial and review
Procedural requests, objections, refusals and their effect
upgrade_dimensions.explanation: The Court records the accused's competing account and counsel-related objection, rather than only the prosecution account. That is affirmative evidence that submissions were considered, but it does not establish comparable disclosure, resources, evidentiary access or opportunity. No material asymmetry or objectively justified distinction can be determined from the reproduced appellate narrative.
upgrade_dimensions.next_verification: Inspect the defence and prosecution submissions and relevant disclosure/request rulings before assigning a level.

missing_facts: Actual public access to the trial hearings
Any exclusion order, scope, ground and necessity
Historical publication/access timing and relevant appeal-hearing form
upgrade_dimensions.explanation: The judgment reports that Mahinay testified in open court, and the reasoned Supreme Court decision is publicly reproduced in the retained source. This supports specific public-facing components, but neither proves the public could attend all relevant trial hearings, that any exclusions were lawful, nor that the judgment was available at its historical issuance. The victim's childhood and privacy concerns could bear on permissible exclusions; they are not proof an exclusion occurred.
upgrade_dimensions.next_verification: Inspect hearing access and any closure orders; distinguish protecting a child victim's privacy from the defendant's juvenile status.
upgrade_dimensions.applicability: Historical prosecution, custodial statement and trial in 1995, followed by Supreme Court automatic review decided 1999-02-01. ICCPR and the 1987 Constitution apply to those events; GC13 (1984) is contemporaneous guidance. GC32 (2007) is used only as a later interpretive aid. ICCPR 14(1); Constitution Article III section 14(2); GC13 paragraph 6; later GC32 paragraphs 28-29. Permitted trial exclusions are stage- and reason-specific.

missing_facts: Exact setting of the police/reporter interview and whether silence followed warnings
Original RTC reasoning and transcript showing the inference's weight
Defence objection and any separate ruling on use of silence
upgrade_dimensions.explanation: The Supreme Court reproduces and relies on trial-court reasoning that persistent silence justifies an inference of non-innocence. Treating failure to protest innocence to police or a reporter as an adverse guilt indicator is a substantial documented concern about the presumption and prosecution burden. The score addresses that express reasoning, not guilt or innocence. The contrary evidence is important: the Court states a beyond-reasonable-doubt circumstantial-evidence test, says prosecution evidence cannot draw strength from a weak defence, and finds independent evidence sufficient. Those holdings do not erase the silence-based reasoning, but the source does not establish whether it was decisive, what warnings applied at the particular interview, or whether a treaty violation was adjudicated.
upgrade_dimensions.next_verification: Have a qualified reviewer compare the original inference, interview circumstances and independent proof with contemporaneous Article III sections 12/14/17 and ICCPR 14(2); reassess if the inference was not applied as reproduced.
upgrade_dimensions.applicability: Historical prosecution, custodial statement and trial in 1995, followed by Supreme Court automatic review decided 1999-02-01. ICCPR and the 1987 Constitution apply to those events; GC13 (1984) is contemporaneous guidance. GC32 (2007) is used only as a later interpretive aid. ICCPR 14(2); Constitution Article III section 14(2); GC13 paragraph 7; later GC32 paragraph 30. A conviction or negative credibility finding alone does not establish this concern.

missing_facts: Arraignment date and record of service/oral explanation
Language understood and language used for formal notice
Actual Information/charge explanation and delivery timing
upgrade_dimensions.explanation: The judgment reports an Information filed on 1995-07-10 charging rape with homicide and a not-guilty plea. Formal charging and a plea show that a criminal charge was presented, but do not prove when Mahinay received its nature, legal basis and alleged acts, in what language, or whether the notice was sufficiently prompt and detailed. The Court's later arrest-reasons guideline (JP0228) is a principle, not a finding that notice was actually provided here, and Article 9 arrest reasons are distinct.
upgrade_dimensions.next_verification: Inspect the retained Information and arraignment/service record if supplied; do not substitute the date of filing for the date the accused learned the charge.
upgrade_dimensions.applicability: Historical prosecution, custodial statement and trial in 1995, followed by Supreme Court automatic review decided 1999-02-01. ICCPR and the 1987 Constitution apply to those events; GC13 (1984) is contemporaneous guidance. GC32 (2007) is used only as a later interpretive aid. ICCPR 14(3)(a); Constitution Article III section 14(2); GC13 paragraph 8; later GC32 paragraph 31. Article 9(2) arrest reasons remain separate.

missing_facts: Counsel appointment and actual preparation time
Disclosure of confession, forensic and witness material
Access to exculpatory material and adjournment requests/rulings
upgrade_dimensions.explanation: The charge was filed in July 1995 and the RTC decision was issued in October 1995, after a trial described in the judgment. Those dates and the ability to advance a competing account do not establish adequate preparation time or facilities. No source describes disclosure, confidential consultation, adjournment requests or access to exculpatory evidence. A roughly three-month filing-to-decision interval can be neither compliance nor undue haste without those facts.
upgrade_dimensions.next_verification: Inspect preparation/disclosure and consultation records; determine complexity and requests rather than inferring adequacy from elapsed time.
upgrade_dimensions.applicability: Historical prosecution, custodial statement and trial in 1995, followed by Supreme Court automatic review decided 1999-02-01. ICCPR and the 1987 Constitution apply to those events; GC13 (1984) is contemporaneous guidance. GC32 (2007) is used only as a later interpretive aid. ICCPR 14(3)(b); Constitution Article III sections 11 and 14; GC13 paragraph 9; later GC32 paragraphs 32-33.

missing_facts: Questioning and conditions from arrest until the lawyer arrived
Original signed warnings/waiver and counsel's complete testimony
Private consultation, actual choice and practical independence
Representation and effectiveness at trial and appeal
upgrade_dimensions.explanation: Mahinay alleged that counsel assisted only when he was forced to sign a confession. If established, token assistance at signature would not satisfy the contemporaneous custodial-counsel safeguards. This supports a specific possible concern, rather than proof of denial. The Court expressly rejected it, relying on the PAO lawyer's testimony that he explained rights before questioning, was present, and explained the waiver in Tagalog. That is the strongest contrary evidence and must remain visible. The reproduction does not resolve any earlier questioning before counsel arrived, confidential advice, choice/independence in practice, or effectiveness through trial and appeal; PAO employment alone proves neither independence nor its absence.
upgrade_dimensions.next_verification: Compare the original interrogation chronology, counsel testimony and signed documents with Article III section 12 and RA7438 section 2(a)-(b); keep the accused's version and the Court's contrary finding distinct.
upgrade_dimensions.applicability: Historical prosecution, custodial statement and trial in 1995, followed by Supreme Court automatic review decided 1999-02-01. ICCPR and the 1987 Constitution apply to those events; GC13 (1984) is contemporaneous guidance. GC32 (2007) is used only as a later interpretive aid. ICCPR 14(3)(b),(d); Constitution Article III sections 11,12,14; RA7438 (1992) section 2(a)-(b). Custodial safeguards affect later trial fairness but are not substituted for a full trial-counsel assessment; later GC32 paragraphs 34 and 37-38.

missing_facts: Attendance at all material stages
Any restriction or absence, notice and justification
Understanding and ability to instruct counsel/respond
upgrade_dimensions.explanation: A not-guilty plea, testimony in open court and presentation of a competing account are documented opportunities to participate. They do not establish attendance or understanding throughout all material hearings, access to counsel when needed, or opportunity to respond to every material allegation. Nothing in the reproduced judgment proves exclusion or an unjustified in-absentia proceeding. An adverse credibility finding about his account is not itself denial of participation.
upgrade_dimensions.next_verification: Inspect relevant attendance and trial records before treating one documented episode as complete meaningful participation.
upgrade_dimensions.applicability: Historical prosecution, custodial statement and trial in 1995, followed by Supreme Court automatic review decided 1999-02-01. ICCPR and the 1987 Constitution apply to those events; GC13 (1984) is contemporaneous guidance. GC32 (2007) is used only as a later interpretive aid. ICCPR 14(3)(d); Constitution Article III section 14(2); GC13 paragraph 11; later GC32 paragraphs 36-37. Absence may be justified only with the relevant notice/opportunity facts.

missing_facts: Cross-examination opportunities and actual scope
Defence witness/evidence requests and rulings
Disclosure and ability to challenge the confession and material witnesses
upgrade_dimensions.explanation: The accused gave a defence account and contested circumstantial evidence and the confession; the Court addressed these objections. That is evidence of contestation, but the reproduction does not show whether material prosecution witnesses were cross-examined, whether relevant defence witnesses could be secured, or whether exclusion/refusal requests caused disadvantage. The appellate credibility deference is a review method, not proof that confrontation was denied.
upgrade_dimensions.next_verification: Inspect the cited trial transcripts and requests/refusals; distinguish a rejected evidential argument from a denied opportunity to present it.
upgrade_dimensions.applicability: Historical prosecution, custodial statement and trial in 1995, followed by Supreme Court automatic review decided 1999-02-01. ICCPR and the 1987 Constitution apply to those events; GC13 (1984) is contemporaneous guidance. GC32 (2007) is used only as a later interpretive aid. ICCPR 14(3)(e); Constitution Article III section 14(2); GC13 paragraph 12; later GC32 paragraph 39. The guarantee does not require admission of every requested witness.

missing_facts: Courtroom language and accused's documented language ability
Any interpretation request, response and interpreter provision
Coverage and adequacy of interpretation at material proceedings
upgrade_dimensions.explanation: The quoted lawyer testimony supports explanation of custodial rights/waiver in Filipino/Tagalog. The reproduction also contains Tagalog questions and answers. These facts do not establish courtroom-language ability, an interpreter need, or adequate free interpretation through trial and review. The English-language reproduction is not proof that the accused understood English, and using Tagalog at custody does not prove he could not understand the courtroom language.
upgrade_dimensions.next_verification: Determine actual language need and court language from supplied trial records; keep the quoted Tagalog passages in their original language and request a verified translation only if necessary.
upgrade_dimensions.applicability: Historical prosecution, custodial statement and trial in 1995, followed by Supreme Court automatic review decided 1999-02-01. ICCPR and the 1987 Constitution apply to those events; GC13 (1984) is contemporaneous guidance. GC32 (2007) is used only as a later interpretive aid. ICCPR 14(3)(f); GC13 paragraph 13; later GC32 paragraph 40. RA7438 section 2(b) language-of-warning requirement is a separate custodial safeguard; nationality alone does not establish interpreter need.

missing_facts: Conditions before counsel arrived and investigation of the alleged threat
Original confession, waiver and full voluntariness testimony
Whether medical access was available and why no certificate was produced
The applicable contemporaneous admissibility/burden ruling and whether independent evidence depended on confession
upgrade_dimensions.explanation: The accused alleged a police threat against his life and a confession signed under pressure; the trial reasoning reproduced by the Court stressed lack of medical proof. A threat can be psychological compulsion without a medical injury, so absence of a certificate alone does not resolve the allegation. claims.text: The Court rejected the seventeen-year-old claim and found the accused more than twenty at the offence.
